encoding.name: Address tag (MASTER)
encoding.semantics: Associated with [ADR_O()]; qualified by [STB_O]; user-defined semantics (e.g. address-size, parity, protected memory).

encoding.name: Data tag, input
encoding.semantics: Associated with [DAT_I()]; qualified by [STB_I]; user-defined (e.g. parity, error correction).

encoding.name: Data tag, output
encoding.semantics: Associated with [DAT_O()]; qualified by [STB_O]; user-defined (e.g. parity, time stamp).

encoding.name: Cycle tag (MASTER)
encoding.semantics: Associated with the Bus Cycle; qualified by [CYC_O]; user-defined (e.g. SINGLE / BLOCK / RMW discriminator, interrupt-ack, cache control).

encoding.name: Cycle tag (SLAVE)
encoding.semantics: Associated with the Bus Cycle; qualified by [CYC_I].

encoding.name: Classic cycle
encoding.semantics: Behaves identically to Wishbone Classic — backwards compatible with non-Registered-Feedback SLAVEs.

encoding.name: Constant address burst cycle
encoding.semantics: Multiple beats to the same ADR_O (FIFO-like).

encoding.name: Incrementing burst cycle
encoding.semantics: Multiple beats to incrementing ADR_O; wrap mode set by BTE_O().

encoding.name: End-of-Burst
encoding.semantics: Asserted on the last beat to signal that the current burst is ending.

tables.name: Burst Type Extension for Incrementing and Decrementing Bursts

encoding.name: Linear burst
encoding.semantics: Address increments by data size each beat, no wrap.

encoding.name: 4-beat wrap burst
encoding.semantics: Address wraps at the (4 * data-size)-byte boundary.

encoding.name: 8-beat wrap burst
encoding.semantics: Address wraps at the (8 * data-size)-byte boundary.

encoding.name: 16-beat wrap burst
encoding.semantics: Address wraps at the (16 * data-size)-byte boundary.

tables.name: Wrap Size address increments (starting-LSBs vs Linear/Wrap-4/Wrap-8)
tables.field_bits: Starting address LSBs (3 bits) -> Linear / Wrap-4 / Wrap-8 next-address sequences

encoding.name: 8-bit port, 8-bit granularity
encoding.semantics: BIG and LITTLE ENDIAN identical. SEL_O()=SEL_O(0) one byte lane.

encoding.name: 16-bit port, 16-bit (WORD) granularity
encoding.semantics: BIG and LITTLE ENDIAN identical at the WORD level.

encoding.name: 32-bit port, 32-bit (DWORD) granularity
encoding.semantics: BIG and LITTLE ENDIAN identical at DWORD level.

tables.name: Cycle termination signals (mutually exclusive per RULE 3.45)

encoding.name: Retry termination
encoding.semantics: Bus not ready; MASTER should retry later (optional).

wishbone_burst_address_equations.Aligned_Address: All beats of a burst SHOULD be aligned per RULE 3.1010 / 3.105 / 3.100 / 3.95 (data organization figures).
wishbone_burst_address_equations.WRAP_boundary: Wrap-4 boundary = 4 * port_size/8 bytes; Wrap-8 boundary = 8 * port_size/8 bytes; Wrap-16 boundary = 16 * port_size/8 bytes
wishbone_burst_address_equations.WRAP_address_n: ADR_O(n+1) = (ADR_O(n) + port_size/8) modulo (wrap_beats * port_size/8) inside the (ADR_start & ~(wrap_boundary - 1))..(+wrap_boundary) range — per Table 4-3.

endianness_definition.BIG_ENDIAN: Byte-lane ordering where the most significant byte is stored at the LOWER address (Section 3.5 Nomenclature). The terms come from Cohen, Danny, 'On Holy Wars and a Plea for Peace', IEEE Computer Magazine, October 1981, pp.49-54, derived from 'Gulliver's Travels' by Jonathan Swift.
endianness_definition.LITTLE_ENDIAN: Byte-lane ordering where the most significant byte is stored at the HIGHER address.

Data tag, input: TGD_I() with DAT_I() / TGD_I() with DAT_I(). Data tag, output: TGD_O() with DAT_O() / TGD_O() with DAT_O(). Cycle tag: TGC_O() with Bus Cycle / TGC_I() with Bus Cycle.
BYTE(N) 8-bit BYTE transfer at address 'N'. WORD(N) 16-bit WORD transfer at address 'N'. DWORD(N) 32-bit Double WORD transfer at address 'N'. QWORD(N) 64-bit Quadruple WORD transfer at address 'N'.
CTI_O(2:0): '000' Classic cycle, '001' Constant address burst cycle, '010' Incrementing burst cycle, '011'-'110' Reserved, '111' End-of-Burst.
BTE_IO(1:0): '00' Linear burst, '01' 4-beat wrap burst, '10' 8-beat wrap burst, '11' 16-beat wrap burst.

evidence.spec_section: 4.4.4 Incrementing Burst Cycle / Wrap Size address increments
evidence.quote: Starting address LSBs - Linear - Wrap-4 - Wrap-8 next-address sequences (000 / 001 / 010 / 011 / 100 / 101 / 110 / 111 starting offsets).

BIG ENDIAN refers to data ordering where the most significant byte is stored at the lower address. LITTLE ENDIAN refers to data ordering where the most significant byte is stored at the higher address. The terms BIG ENDIAN and LITTLE ENDIAN for data organization was coined by Danny Cohen of the Information Sciences Institute, and was derived from the book Gulliver's Travels by Jonathan Swift.
